title: Story mode in a futuristic racer?
author: ActionLittle4176
selftext:
Seven months into my futuristic racer, and I’m still working on giving it an identity of its own (especially now that making a futuristic racer has become something of a vibecoding rite of passage).

One of the things Street Fighter II brought to fighting games was a personal story for each character, which gave context and purpose to what would otherwise just be two people hitting each other. That backstory is also a big part of why the cast had so much personality.

In the same spirit, I want my game to be character-driven, with pilots who are more than a face to put on a ship. So I’m trying out a story mode. Essentially: a shared intro that sets up the game’s lore, then a personal arc for each pilot with its own intro, short cinematic scenes between races, and an ending. I have a few other ideas I’m weighing for later.

![img](vlve83s9rg0i1 "Yuki in the pilot selection screen")

For now I’ve built the campaign for one pilot, Yuki. It still has a few small inconsistencies to fix, the kind you get with Seedance (the video model I’m using for the cinematics), but I think the format comes across. The plan is to do this for the six starting characters (Seedance isn’t cheap) and, if the game ever pays for itself, keep adding campaigns for the rest. You can try it in the open beta at [https://fm1.app](https://fm1.app), but I’m also posting Yuki’s story as a video so you can watch it without playing.

What do you think? Does a mode like this make a futuristic racer more appealing to you, or is it effort the genre doesn’t need? And once you’ve watched Yuki’s story, do you see her any differently than just a face in the pilot selection screen?

PS: Yes, the story ends on a cliffhanger. Once each pilot’s campaign is done, the plan is a new tournament shared by all of them, where things get a lot more fantastical and weird, but fun.
